Jever now supports local decision models through [Ollaya](https://ollaya.dev/), alongside TypeSafe Jev through OpenRouter.

### Downloads

| Platform                             | Download                    |
| ------------------------------------ | --------------------------- |
| macOS — Apple Silicon (M1 and later) | `Jever-0.0.2-mac-arm64.dmg` |
| macOS — Intel                        | `Jever-0.0.2-mac-x64.dmg`   |
| Windows — x64                        | `Jever-0.0.2-win-x64.exe`   |

The macOS ZIP files contain the same app as the DMG installers. `SHA256SUMS.txt` contains checksums for all installers and ZIP files.

### In this release

- Choose Ollaya or OpenRouter in **Settings → Connection**, with the active provider and model visible in the conversation header.
- Connect to a local or remote Ollaya server, discover installed models, and select a custom model.
- Run Choice, Score, and yes/no decisions without an API key on a default local Ollaya server.
- Save optional Ollaya authentication securely, separately from OpenRouter and scoped to the server URL.
- See a warning when Ollaya truncates input, with model routing and timing metadata preserved in response details and backups.
- Use up to 256 questions, 255 choices per question, and 10 score levels with Ollaya, subject to the model's context budget and Jever's request-size limit.
- Allow up to 10 minutes for requests that need extra model-loading time.
- Import choice label arrays in the JSON editor and use question IDs when instructions are omitted.

Existing workspaces retain their conversations and OpenRouter connection. OpenRouter support is unchanged.

### Get started with Ollaya

Install [Ollaya](https://ollaya.dev/download), pull a model with `ollaya pull laya`, and start the server with `ollaya serve` if it is not already running.

In Jever, select **Settings → Connection → Ollaya**, use `http://localhost:11435` and model `laya`, then save and click **Test & refresh models**. Jever uses models installed on the server; it does not download weights. If your server requires authentication, save its API key in the Ollaya connection settings.

### Verification and installation notes

The integration passes 63 automated tests. Real Laya inference, model discovery, and persistence after restart were verified on macOS with Ollaya 0.6.0. Other model families and hardware configurations have not been verified.

These are early, unsigned distribution builds. The macOS apps are ad-hoc signed but not Apple-notarized; macOS may block opening them. Windows may show an unknown-publisher or SmartScreen warning. Install only if you trust this repository and its artifacts.

Automated tests and production builds run for each target. Packaging success does not verify every desktop interaction on each operating system.
